battle.name: 大哥倫比亞-秘魯戰爭
battle.theater: 秘魯中部高原與厄瓜多爾南部海岸
battle.brief: 一八二八年夏，秘魯制憲議會選出加馬拉為總統、宣告脫離邦聯，大哥倫比亞斷絕邦交、陳兵厄瓜多爾南部；一八二九年一月揚貝利海戰未分勝負，陸軍自洛哈越境，於瓜馬斯山口擊潰秘魯主力，同日蘇克雷在胡寧擊敗保王軍。本卡長槍早已退下戰場，方陣的密度與抗騎兵邏輯由刺刀線與騎槍繼承。

kit.name: 長槍
kit.history: 方陣的長矛讓火槍隊站在後面。密西西比之後，長矛和火槍一起站住了。

countries: 這是一場兩個新興國家在西班牙帝國崩解後互相清算的戰爭，戰線同時在安第斯山中部高原與厄瓜多爾南部海岸展開。聯邦一方是大哥倫比亞：一八一九年由新格拉納達、委內瑞拉與基多聯合而成，首都波哥大，總統兼最高統帥西蒙·玻利瓦爾，下轄以波哥大、基多兩地軍校訓練出來的線列步兵為骨幹的野戰軍，以及由英籍海軍出身的伊靈沃思·亨特指揮、駐紮瓜亞基爾的太平洋分艦隊。另一方是秘魯邦聯中的「秘魯國」：一八二一年聖馬丁渡過安第斯山、攻入利馬後建立的國家，一八二六年與上瓦爾帕拉索地區成立的玻利維亞國組成秘魯—玻利維亞邦聯，設最高總監於庫斯科；秘魯一方以利馬的制憲議會、總統府、國民軍與各省民兵為骨架，並與仍據安第斯中部、以佩德羅·德·拉·塞爾納親王為首的保王軍殘部結盟，用以對抗聯邦。玻利維亞自身也瀕臨分裂，總統烏爾迪內亞在聯邦壓力下辭職，軍隊與歲入被秘魯吸走，國家實權逐步落到安德烈斯·聖克魯斯手中。兩邊都沒有外國正規軍直接參戰，兵員以本國常備軍與民兵為限，勝負全在山上與海上。
countriesEn: This was a war in which two young states settled accounts with each other after the collapse of the Spanish empire, fought simultaneously in the highlands of the central Andes and off the southern coast of Ecuador. On the confederation side stood Gran Colombia: created in 1819 from New Granada, Venezuela and Quito, with its capital at Bogotá, its president and supreme commander Simón Bolívar, a field army built on close-order infantry trained in the military schools of Bogotá and Quito, and a Pacific squadron stationed at Guayaquil under the English-born John Illingworth Hunt. On the other side was the State of Peru within the Peru-Bolivian Confederation: the state created in 1821 when San Martín crossed the Andes and entered Lima, which in 1826 joined with the new state of Bolivia on the upper coast to form the confederation, with a Supreme Director seated at Cusco. The Peruvian side was organised around the constituent congress in Lima, the presidency, the national army and the provincial militias, and it allied itself with the remaining royalist army of the central Andes under the viceroy Pedro de la Serna in order to face the confederation. Bolivia itself was coming apart: its president Urdininea resigned under confederate pressure, its troops and revenues were drained away by Peru, and real power passed gradually to Andrés de Santa Cruz. Neither side had foreign regular armies fighting directly, and the numbers on both sides were limited to their own national troops and militias; everything was decided on the heights and at sea.
people: 關鍵人物是西蒙·玻利瓦爾與阿古斯丁·加馬拉。玻利瓦爾是邦聯計劃的設計者：作為邦聯最高總監，他主張把秘魯與玻利維亞合為一國、共用軍隊財政、把首府設在基多，並要求解散秘魯國民軍交由邦聯軍接管；一八二八年秘魯單方面退出後，他以大哥倫比亞總統兼陸軍總司令身分拒絕承認，下令坎特羅率軍進軍。玻利維亞總統何塞·瑪麗亞·佩雷斯·德·烏爾迪內亞被迫辭職，安德烈斯·聖克魯斯接任並在下一年走向獨立。加馬拉是秘魯一方的支柱：這位軍人出身的考迪羅一八二六年曾被玻利瓦爾任命為最高總監，一八二七年被政變推翻，一八二八年六月當選秘魯總統後立刻拒絕邦聯的接管權，拒絕解散自己的軍隊，率軍在曼塔羅河谷迎戰，八月六日戰死。拉蒙·卡斯蒂利亞以臨時總統身分接手善後，並主持接納亞克欽戰後的保王軍。秘魯方面還有里維亞-阿格羅，這位曾任邦聯秘魯代表、力主維持兩國獨立的總統在衝突爆發前已下台。蘇克雷是大哥倫比亞北線的指揮者，在胡寧與亞克欽兩役打垮保王軍，威廉·米勒任其參謀長；坎特拉率領的保王軍在胡寧敗後退入山區。海軍方面，伊靈沃思·亨特率大哥倫比亞分艦隊作戰，利薩多·蒙特羅與曼紐埃爾·比列加爾代表秘魯海軍。玻利瓦爾本人於一八二九年十二月十七日在聖馬爾塔病逝。
peopleEn: The two key figures are Simón Bolívar and Agustín Gamarra. Bolívar was the architect of the confederation scheme: as Supreme Director he wanted Peru and Bolivia merged into a single state with a common army and treasury and the capital at Quito, and he demanded that the Peruvian national army be dissolved and handed to the confederate army; when Peru withdrew unilaterally in 1828 he refused to recognise it in his capacity as president of Gran Colombia and commander-in-chief of its army, and ordered Cantero to advance. José María Pérez de Urdininea, president of Bolivia, was forced to resign, and Andrés de Santa Cruz took over and would lead the country to independence the following year. Gamarra was the pillar of the Peruvian side: this soldier-caudillo had himself been appointed Supreme Director by Bolívar in 1826, was overthrown in a coup in 1827, and after being elected president of Peru in June 1828 immediately rejected the confederate claim of authority, refused to disband his own army, took the field in the Mantaro valley, and was killed on 6 August. Ramón Castilla took over as provisional president to settle the aftermath and presided over the reception of the royalist army after Ayacucho. On the Peruvian side too was Riva-Agüero, the former confederate delegate for Peru who had argued for keeping the two states independent and had already been removed from office before the conflict broke out. Sucre commanded the northern Gran Colombian line and destroyed the royalist army at Junín and Ayacucho, with Guillermo Miller as his chief of staff; Canterac's royalists retreated into the mountains after Junín. At sea, John Illingworth Hunt led the Gran Colombian squadron, and Lizardo Montero and Manuel Villar spoke for the Peruvian navy. Bolívar himself died of illness at Santa Marta on 17 December 1829.
kits: 本卡兵器是十六世紀西班牙方陣的長槍：三米上下的硬木槍桿、鐵製槍頭，槍手居中排成長廊，兩翼由火槍手與弩手掩護，槍與火槍合成同一個火力單位。到了一八二九年，這件兵器早已退下戰場：歐洲各國的野戰部隊都已棄用長槍，俄國是唯一仍在線列中保留槍兵的國家，但遠在安第斯山之外。它在這場戰爭留下三種痕跡。其一是制度上的：大哥倫比亞與秘魯的新軍都由西班牙舊制民兵改編而來，營制、操典與連隊編分仍沿用方陣時代的「槍兵—火槍」格局，軍校教程仍以密集方陣為核心科目。其二是功能上的：長槍的直接後裔是騎槍，大哥倫比亞的近衛隊與長槍騎兵團以三米以上長矛作戰，秘魯與玻利維亞騎兵同樣用矛，這正是方陣抗騎兵邏輯的騎兵版本；一八二九年蘇克雷在胡寧與亞克欽都靠方陣與騎槍對付保王軍騎兵。其三是象徵上的：方陣（cuadrado）的概念仍被口頭強調，密度與刺刀的習慣留在線列步兵身上。實際裝備方面，雙方步兵是燧發滑膛火槍加刺刀的線列營，配野戰砲與山砲；騎兵配彎刀、馬槍與長矛；後勤靠騾隊、驢隊與牛車，越過安第斯山隘口時靠馱騡與口糧配給；保王軍另有一批西班牙舊式銅砲，亞克欽後成為秘魯軍的繳獲。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the pike of the sixteenth-century Spanish tercia: a shaft of some three metres of hardwood tipped with an iron point, the pikemen standing in the centre as a dense corridor with musketeers and crossbowmen covering the flanks, so that pike and shot formed a single unit of fire. By 1829 that equipment had long left the field of battle: every European field army had abandoned the pike, and Russia was the only country still keeping pikemen in the line, and Russia was nowhere near the Andes. Yet the pike leaves three traces in this war. The first is institutional: the new armies of both Gran Colombia and Peru were converted from the old Spanish militia, and their organisation, their drill manuals and their company structure still followed the tercia pattern of pike and musket, while the military schools still taught the dense square as a core subject. The second is functional: the direct heir of the pike is the lance, and Gran Colombia's guard and lancer regiments fought with lances of more than three metres while Peruvian and Bolivian horse carried them too; that was the mounted version of the square's anti-cavalry logic, and in 1829 Sucre used square and lance against the royalist horse at both Junín and Ayacucho. The third is symbolic: the concept of the square (cuadrado) was still on everyone's lips, and its habits of density and of the bayonet survived in the close-order infantry. As for the actual equipment, the infantry of both sides were close-order battalions of flintlock smoothbore muskets with bayonets, with field and mountain guns; the horse carried sabres, carbines and lances; supply rested on mule, donkey and ox trains, and pack animals and rationing carried the army over the Andean passes; the royalists had a battery of old Spanish bronze guns, which fell to Peru as booty after Ayacucho.
tactics: 大哥倫比亞的戰略是一面斷絕秘魯與玻利維亞的聯繫，一面以海軍封鎖派塔等港、阻止軍火流入，同時讓陸軍沿洛哈—亞巴卡通道越過安第斯，奪取曼塔羅河谷，再向亞克欽與利馬推進。海軍方面，一八二九年一月二十五日揚貝利海戰中，大哥倫比亞分艦隊以旗艦「總統號」為核心嘗試強行進入瓜亞基爾灣，登上揚貝利島後登岸受挫，與秘魯巡防艦隊在夜間近距離互射至天明，雙方各有斬獲，最終聯邦分艦隊退回瓜亞基爾，戰役未分勝負。陸軍方面，坎特羅的縱隊自洛哈經亞巴卡越過三千米以上的高山隘口，補給線拉長至數百公里，糧秣靠馱騡輸送；兵鋒進入萬卡約與豪恩加之間的曼塔羅河谷後，加馬拉的守軍在谷口布防，聯邦軍以線列射擊與刺刀衝鋒正面壓破，秘魯中路崩潰，加馬拉在重整隊形時陣亡，聯邦軍隨即攻入萬卡約與豪恩加。北線方面，蘇克雷在海拔四千米的胡寧高原與坎特拉的保王騎兵交鋒，長槍騎兵與獵騎兵反覆衝鋒，擊潰保王軍騎兵；其後蘇克雷翻越安第斯南下，於一八二九年十二月九日亞克欽的克蘇拉山一線佔據高地，與保王軍正面決戰，最後以方陣頂住西班牙騎兵、以刺刀衝鋒解決戰鬥，拉塞爾納親王投降。戰局未定之際，未領到糧餉的大哥倫比亞軍隊在亞克欽宣布總罷工，佔領區迅速瓦解，聯邦軍於一八二九年十二月起陸續撤退。
tacticsEn: The Gran Colombian plan was to cut Peru off from Bolivia while the navy blockaded ports such as Paita to keep arms out, and at the same time to let the land army cross the Andes by the Loja-Ayabaca route, seize the Mantaro valley and press on toward Ayacucho and Lima. At sea, in the naval battle of Jambelí on 25 January 1829, the Gran Colombian squadron, built around its flagship Presidente, tried to force its way into the Gulf of Guayaquil, landed on the island of Jambelí and was repulsed ashore, and then exchanged fire at close range with the Peruvian squadron through the night until dawn, each side claiming captures, before the confederate squadron fell back to Guayaquil; the action was undecided. On land, Cantero's column crossed the Andean passes above three thousand metres by way of Loja and Ayabaca, the supply line stretching to several hundred kilometres, with rations carried on pack animals; once the head of the column reached the Mantaro valley between Huancayo and Jauja, Gamarra's army deployed at the entrance to the valley, and the Gran Colombians broke them head-on with linear fire and the bayonet charge. The Peruvian centre collapsed, Gamarra was killed while trying to rally his troops, and the Gran Colombians stormed Huancayo and Jauja. In the north, Sucre met Canterac's royalist horse on the Junín plateau at four thousand metres, where the lancers and cazadores charged again and again and broke the royalist cavalry; Sucre then crossed the Andes to the south and fought the decisive action at Ayacucho on 9 December 1829, taking the heights of the Condor mountain, matching the royalists in a set-piece battle, holding off the Spanish horse with the square and ending the day with a bayonet charge that decided everything, until Viceroy La Serna surrendered. Before the outcome was settled, the unpaid Gran Colombian troops in Ayacucho declared a general strike, the occupied districts fell apart, and the confederate army began withdrawing in December 1829.
data: 雙方兵數各來源記載不一，較接近的說法是：坎特羅率領的大哥倫比亞入侵部隊約三千至四千人，以步兵、騎兵與砲隊為主；加馬拉在瓜馬斯山口迎戰的秘魯軍約兩千五百至三千人。北線胡寧之戰，蘇克雷所部約兩千五百至三千人，坎特拉約兩千人上下；亞克欽之戰，蘇克雷一方約兩千五百至三千人，拉塞爾納一方不足兩千人。雙方陣亡與被俘的具體數字缺乏可靠統計，僅有亞克欽一役戰後大批保王軍官兵被俘、軍械盡為秘魯繳獲的概略記載。地理與時間：基多至萬卡約陸路約三百公里，亞巴卡一線的隘口海拔逾三千米，萬卡約海拔約三千二百七十米，亞克欽約二千七百六十米，胡寧高原約四千一百米；瓜亞基爾至揚貝利一段航程數百公里，聯邦分艦隊的封鎖自一八二九年春延續至年底。經濟上，爭奪的標的包括瓦利加的鹽礦、瓜亞基爾海關收入與邦聯債務分攤；大哥倫比亞的國庫在戰後耗盡，軍官與士兵欠餉達數月之久。
dataEn: Sources differ on the numbers involved, and the figures closest to the mark are these: Cantero's invading Gran Colombian force numbered about three to four thousand, built on infantry, cavalry and guns; the Peruvian army Gamarra brought to the Portada de Guamas was around two and a half to three thousand men. At Junín in the north, Sucre had roughly two and a half to three thousand men against Canterac's some two thousand; at Ayacucho, Sucre's side numbered about two and a half to three thousand while La Serna had fewer than two thousand. There is no reliable count of the dead and captured on either side, and only a general sense that after Ayacucho large numbers of royalist officers and men were taken prisoner and their guns fell to Peru. Geography and time: some three hundred kilometres of road separate Quito from Huancayo, the passes on the Ayabaca line stand above three thousand metres, Huancayo lies at about 3,270 metres, Ayacucho at about 2,760 and the Junín plateau at about 4,100; the passage from Guayaquil to Jambelí is several hundred kilometres, and the confederate blockade ran from the spring of 1829 to the end of the year. Financially, the stakes were the salt mines of Huallaga, the customs revenues of Guayaquil and the apportionment of the confederate debt; the Gran Colombian treasury was empty after the war, and officers and soldiers went months without pay.
cause: 戰爭的根子是秘魯—玻利維亞邦聯自一八二六年五月庫斯科條約建立起的那一刻便設計脆弱：兩個國家、一位最高總監、一支合編軍隊、一個共用國庫，卻各自保留國號、議會與軍隊，權責無從劃分。玻利瓦爾主張合邦、遷都基多、並把秘魯國民軍併入邦聯軍，秘魯的精英與制憲議會則視之為玻利維亞藉並吞秘魯、獨佔鹽礦與海關的捷徑；曾任邦聯秘魯代表的里維亞-阿格羅因主張維持兩國獨立而被罷免，成為分離派的精神象徵。一八二七年玻利瓦爾把最高總監駐地移至利馬並親自坐鎮，令利馬疑心玻利維亞軍隊隨時會進城接管政權，兩國的裂痕遂從條文延伸到軍隊與稅收。直接導火線是一八二八年六月的秘魯制憲議會：議會選出加馬拉為總統，等於宣告邦聯名存實亡；大哥倫比亞以驅逐駐瓜亞基爾的秘魯守軍、召回邦聯軍人、派坎特羅集結兵力回應，秘魯則拉攏仍據山區的保王軍殘部共同抵抗。於是，一場關於邦聯契約的分裂，最終以兩個共和國的兵戎相見收場。
causeEn: The root of the war lay in the fact that the Peru-Bolivian Confederation was fragile from the moment it was created by the Treaty of Cusco in May 1826: two countries, one Supreme Director, one merged army and one common treasury, yet each retained its own name, assembly and army, and nobody could define who was responsible for what. Bolívar wanted union, the capital at Quito and the Peruvian national army folded into the confederate army, while the Peruvian elite and the constituent congress read the whole scheme as a road by which Bolivia would swallow Peru and take the salt mines and the customs for itself; Riva-Agüero, who had served as the confederate delegate for Peru and had argued for keeping the two states independent, was removed from office and became the emblem of separation. In 1827 Bolívar moved the seat of the Supreme Director to Lima and sat there in person, and Lima came to fear that the Bolivian army might march into the capital and take over; the rift between the two states spread from the clauses of the treaty to their armies and their taxes. The immediate trigger was the Peruvian constituent congress of June 1828: the assembly elected Gamarra president, which amounted to declaring the confederation a dead letter. Gran Colombia answered by driving out the Peruvian garrison at Guayaquil, recalling the confederate servicemen and massing Cantero's troops, while Peru drew in the surviving royalist army of the highlands to resist. What began as a dispute over the terms of a confederation thus ended with two republics in arms against each other.
impact: 這場戰爭同時結束了兩件事：秘魯—玻利維亞邦聯與玻利瓦爾的大陸計劃。秘魯保住了國家存續與主權，代價是國力耗盡、軍隊膨脹、並接收了整支保王軍殘部與其軍械，一八二九年之後的「亞克欽一代」將在秘魯政壇上支配數十年，一八三〇年代連續出現軍事共和國，國家制度的走向從此長期受考迪羅與軍人集團擺布。玻利維亞則在聖克魯斯帶領下走向獨立，一八三一年制憲議會確認其脫離秘魯，此後它與秘魯在塔克納與阿里卡一帶的邊界糾紛成為南美洲最持久的衝突源頭，最終在一八三七至一八三八年、一八五二年的塔克納佔領以及一八七九至一八八四年的太平洋戰爭中爆發；玻利維亞正是因這場戰爭失去海岸而永久淪為內陸國。對大哥倫比亞而言，這是一場打贏了戰役卻輸了國家的戰爭：國庫枯竭、軍隊罷工、玻利瓦爾病逝，委內瑞拉與厄瓜多爾相繼分離，一八三〇至一八三一年大哥倫比亞解體，整個南美大陸共和國的構想就此終結。
impactEn: This war ended two things at once: the Peru-Bolivian Confederation and Bolívar's continental project. Peru kept its national existence and its sovereignty, at the price of an exhausted treasury, an inflated army and the absorption of the entire surviving royalist force with its guns; the generation of Ayacucho would dominate Peruvian politics for decades, military republics followed one another through the 1830s, and the direction of the state's institutions was henceforth at the mercy of caudillos and military factions. Bolivia, led by Santa Cruz, went its own way and became independent, its constituent congress confirming the break with Peru in 1831; the border disputes with Peru over Tacna and Arica would then become the most persistent source of conflict in South America, breaking out in 1837-38, in the seizure of Tacna in 1852 and finally in the War of the Pacific of 1879-1884, in which Bolivia lost the coast and was permanently reduced to a landlocked state. For Gran Colombia this was a war won on the battlefield and lost as a state: the treasury was empty, the army struck, Bolívar died, Venezuela and Ecuador separated in turn, and Gran Colombia came apart in 1830-31, ending the idea of a single continental republic for South America.
result: 軍事上，大哥倫比亞贏得了多數戰役：揚貝利海戰未分勝負，瓜馬斯山口擊敗加馬拉、迫其陣亡，胡寧打垮坎特拉的保王騎兵，亞克欽更迫使拉塞爾納親王與整支保王軍投降，秘魯從此再無可用的王軍。戰略上，大哥倫比亞卻輸得一塌糊塗：入侵部隊深入安第斯山中部，補給線越拉越長，未領到糧餉的軍隊於亞克欽宣布總罷工，玻利瓦爾又在聖馬爾塔病逝，消息傳回後士兵拒絕作戰，聯邦軍在一八二九年十二月起分批撤出秘魯，戰果與佔地全部吐回。政治上，秘魯維護了國家主權與邦聯解體的目標，卻也從此背負一支龐大的軍人階層，國政落入考迪羅與亞克欽一代手中；玻利維亞在聖克魯斯掌權後分立，一八三一年成為獨立國家並在十年內成為秘魯最兇猛的對手；大哥倫比亞則在罷工、分離與財政崩潰中解體，那面曾把方陣與火槍綁在一起的長槍旗幟，也隨之從安第斯山麓撤下。
resultEn: Militarily Gran Colombia won most of the engagements: Jambelí was undecided, the Portada de Guamas defeated Gamarra and killed him, Junín broke Canterac's royalist horse, and Ayacucho forced Viceroy La Serna and the whole royalist army to surrender, after which Peru had no royalist force left to use. Strategically, however, Gran Colombia lost the war outright: its invading columns pushed deep into the central Andes, the supply line grew longer and longer, the unpaid troops declared a general strike at Ayacucho, and Bolívar fell ill and died at Santa Marta; when the news reached the front the men refused to fight, the confederate army began withdrawing from Peru in December 1829 in detachments, and every gain and every occupied district was handed back. Politically Peru preserved its sovereignty and the dissolution of the confederation, but it inherited a heavy military caste whose weight would govern the country, and the affairs of the state passed into the hands of the caudillos and the generation of Ayacucho; Bolivia, under Santa Cruz, went separate and became an independent state in 1831, and within a decade the most dangerous opponent Peru had ever had; and Gran Colombia dissolved amid strike, secession and financial ruin, taking down with it the banner that had once bound the square to the musket.
